title: Who has a customer chat
summary: A line at the top of a customer chat of a work account with two or more people (bipe ADR 0284 points 15 to 17): who has the chat, its status, Pegar, Passar, Devolver and Notas. Customers see nothing of it.

assignee.description: Seat ID of the assignee. Absent: the chat is in the pool.

assigneeName.description: Name of that seat from the seat list.

status.description: ChatAssignmentStatus. open when there is no record.

phase.description: taken: another person has the chat, shows bipe_chat_taken_banner. failed shows bipe_chat_assign_error.

take.effect: PUT /v1/me/business/chats/{roomId} with assignee_seat_id = mySeat and expected_assignee_seat_id = assignee. 409 chat_taken: reads the chats again and shows taken.

seat.description: Seat ID picked from the active seats, under bipe_chat_give_title.

give.effect: PUT with assignee_seat_id = seat and expected_assignee_seat_id = assignee.

release.effect: PUT with assignee_seat_id null and expected_assignee_seat_id = assignee.

setStatus.effect: PUT with the current assignee in both fields and the new status.

reply.effect: Before the first send in a chat in the pool, take runs. In a chat another person has, the composer shows bipe_chat_taken_reply first. After each send, sends the reply-by event (registries/work-notes.json) to the notes room.

notes: Inside the account, a reply to the customer shows bipe_chat_reply_by with the seat name when a valid reply-by event names it (replyByFromEvent, test-vectors/work-notes.json). With none, the reply shows no name.
The record is a help to divide work, not a lock: a person can always reply after bipe_chat_taken_reply.
With one person, this line does not show.
